1.30.0 Generic templating. Using the distpy.io_help.io_helpers.template function. The input parameter is a dictionary, templateJSON containing two terms, the filename - which is the                  path to the template, and the variables - a list of key-value pairs,                  everywhere the string in the key occurs it is substituted by the string                  in the value.

1.29.0 Create a generic interface for the ingesters, so that the code can be rationalized to have just one parallel_ingest. The previous ingesters use the refactored solution and provided a depracation message. This also enabled an alternative approach to processing where data is ingested to memory rather  than a "hot" storage. This configuration is useful in the low storage environments such as laptops or edge devices. Multiprocessing is available in the new configuration similarly to the old one.
1.28.0 Added the time domain dip-filter command. This uses the scipy.ndimage.convolve which is now under the extra_numpy convolve2D function so that it can be later upgraded to be GPU compatible.

1.24.1 Improved the behaviour when an unknown command is used. This can happen if the JSON file has an error in it, or more often when a workflow that uses a proprietary extension is run on a system where that extension is not installed. Now returns an empty BasicCommand - so the input feeds directly to the output and all the automatic documentation works.

1.22.0 Improved the automatic documentation. Now you can define a "comment" field on a command - which will appear instead of the command name in the graph representation. You can also define "formatting" which accepts any dot graph formatting sting, so colours fonts and styles all become available for this graph representation.

1.18.0 Generalized the kmeans clustering so that one can supply multiple processed data types as the input. So there are two modes, if you have multiple data-types then the assumption is that you want to clusters across (x,t). If you send one datatype then you want clusters in either x or t.
